We are a dedicated team focused on improving access to affordable prescription medications for patients. By partnering with insurance companies, healthcare providers, and pharmacies, we work to reduce the financial burden of medications, ensuring that patients can access the treatments they need without excessive costs.

  • Program Renewal & Updates: Guide patients through annual renewals and inform them about any updates to the program or medication formulary.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Experience in healthcare, insurance or customer service required (experience with prescription assistance programs is a plus)

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.

  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

Nice to have

 

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure

Terms

 

  • US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms

The garden3d technology story

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Who you are

Theyâre flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work âsmartâ by carefully managing their workflow and team.

If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. This is as much an operations role as a reporting one. You will translate what the business needs to know into what the data platform has to deliver, working with our Data Engineers on the production and quality data in the lakehouse and turning it into the reporting used across three European plants, including our Digital Shopfloor Management Solution, relied on by more than 300 people. You will also go to where the data is created and make it better there — improving how it is captured, automating what is still manual, and helping three plants work to one standard.

At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our operations span multiple plants and teams, and your work will directly support the reliability, efficiency, and excellence required for mission-critical production. Join us in shaping the next era of aerospace operations.

  • Be the go-to contact between the business owners of production and quality data — plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on.

  • Own the production and quality domain in our lakehouse: know which tables and fields hold what, where each comes from, and who owns it at source — and keep that knowledge documented rather than in your head.
  • Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for production and quality: specify the tables, fields, and business rules the business needs, and validate the result against what actually happens on the shopfloor before anyone relies on it.
  • Set and monitor data quality checks for your domain, and route each issue to the right owner — the person entering the data, the system configuration, or the pipeline — until it is fixed.
  • Maintain and continuously improve Power BI dashboards tracking production and quality performance across all three plants, built on certified lakehouse data rather than side spreadsheets.
  • Describe production and quality data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first.
  • Automate what is manual today: recurring reports, data collection, and the preparation behind daily and weekly performance routines.
  • Support the standardisation of ways of working across the three plants, partnering with our Lean Operations Specialist so that measurement and improvement pull in the same direction.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Quality Management, or a related field.

  • Strong expertise in Power BI (data modeling, DAX, dashboard design, troubleshooting), complemented by advanced Excel skills.
  • Comfortable querying data with SQL and working in a lakehouse or data warehouse environment; experience with Microsoft Fabric or a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture is a plus. You will not build the pipelines — you need to know what to ask for and how to check what comes back.

  • A track record of improving or automating a process, not only reporting on it. Exposure to continuous improvement methods is a plus.
  • Comfortable working across multiple sites and collaborating with production teams, quality engineers, and leadership alike.
  • Fluent in English; Spanish, German or Dutch is a strong plus given our plant locations.
  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred.

Who You Are

You are equally comfortable on a shopfloor and in a data model, and you speak both languages — the plant's and the lakehouse's. You know that the fastest way to fix a reporting problem is often to walk to the place where the data is created and ask how it gets entered — and then change it.

You are structured and persistent, because aligning three plants on one way of working takes more than a good spreadsheet; it takes patience and conversations. You enjoy the detail of a root cause but stay focused on whether performance actually improved, and when something is manual or repetitive you would rather automate it than live with it.

You turn numbers into stories, stories into priorities, and priorities into measurable change. Above all, you take ownership, challenge assumptions, and stay committed to operational excellence.

jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As a member of our Security Operations Team, you will collaborate with a global team of engineers to monitor and respond to security events, lead security incidents as Incident Commander, and lead digital forensic investigations in support of Employee Relations, Legal, Compliance, or Information Security cases.

Although you will be focused on security incident response, you will also have the opportunity to create and maintain runbooks, and automated workflows, and assist in process refinement and implementation. You will collaborate with a diverse team of engineers, and key stakeholders on security initiatives across the company. Above all, your focus is bringing Security expertise to the table in a collaborative, humble, and practical manner.

Location: This role is open to candidates residing in the UK

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will: 

  • Monitor security events and provide technical analysis on alerts
  • Lead information security incidents and employee insider investigations by developing the incident response strategy, lead the execution through incident closure, while providing incident updates to key stakeholders throughout the incident
  • Deliver security guidance clearly and concisely for incident response and insider threat initiatives
  • Coordinate the building of services, capabilities, integrations, and implementations of technologies to support security operations, incident response, and insider threat
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
  • Participate in our on-call rota covering weekends

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years of experience in Security Incident Response
  • Ability to communicate investigative findings and strategies to technical staff, executive leadership, and legal
  • Ability to build scripts or tools to support Samsara's investigation processes, with proficiency in Python
  • Mentor and train security operation engineers on data collection, analysis, and reporting technical analysis
  • Practical experience acting as a lead during security incident response, including monitoring and triaging alerts, and coordinating across teams
  • Understanding of analysis and forensics techniques on macOS, Windows, and Linux
  • Experience utilizing SIEM tools to perform log reviews
  • Experience in cloud architecture and security (AWS, GCP) and cloud-based services
  • Participation in an on-call rotation, with the potential to work outside standard business hours, including late evenings, when responding to high-severity incidents as part of our global incident response team.
  • This role will be part of our EMEA so your hours will be aligned to the UK. As an operational time you may be expected to work flexible hours around this to support the load of the team

An ideal candidate also has:

  • 2+ years of experience working on insider threat initiatives or employee investigations
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field - or relevant industry experience
  • GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH) or similar Certification
  • Familiarity with common security frameworks and standards, including NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, FedRAMP

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

jobs.title: Senior Business Controller (Operations)
jobs.description:
Would you like to work closely with the business as a Senior Business Controller and use your financial expertise to make a real impact on decisions? You will bring financial structure and insight, while keeping a forward-looking perspective: where can we improve, which decisions will make a financial difference, and what will they mean for our results?

HG is a compact, international organisation. This means considerable responsibility, direct contact with decision-makers and room to drive change yourself. We are therefore looking for someone who takes ownership, works pragmatically and is not afraid to challenge existing ways of working.

You will be based at our head office in Almere. Hybrid working opportunities are limited: regular office attendance is important in this role because of the close collaboration with Finance, Operations and other stakeholders. You will also travel to the United Kingdom or Germany several times a year.

About the role

As Senior Business Controller, you will be responsible for business control within Operations and will also support our subsidiaries in the United Kingdom and Germany. You have a clear vision of what the best operational business control model looks like and have proven experience in realizing this. The Senior Business Controller plays a key role in strengthening financial control, transparency and decision-making across Operations. The scope covers procurement and product costing, as well as warehouse and transport operations. Working closely with Finance, Procurement and Operations, the Senior Business Controller translates operational developments and improvement initiatives into clear financial insights and P&L impact

Our business is undergoing significant change. HG has recently changed its logistics service arrangements, consolidating most local warehouses into one central location as part of a cost-saving initiative. At the same time, a new ERP system is being implemented. This creates an interesting and dynamic environment in which existing budget models, cost allocation models, reporting and financial processes need to be further developed to reflect the new operating model and provide a solid basis for financial control and decision-making.

What you will do

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Owning the operational cost lines between Net Sales and Contribution Margin for the whole group and. act as a strong Finance business partner to the Chief Operating Officer and his team, translating operational developments into actionable financial insights;

  • Identifying and driving continuous improvements to the operational business, improving insights while reducing costs.

  • Being the financial business partner for the country managers in the UK and Germany, including reviewing commercial deals and business cases.

  • Analyzing budget versus actuals and explaining significant variances.

  • Developing a clear understanding of budgeted versus actual purchase prices and identifying the key drivers behind price variances.

  • Providing insight into raw material and purchase price developments and translating these into expected P&L impact.

  • Quantifying and tracking the financial impact of Procurement and product-costing initiatives and other savings programmes.

  • Establishing and further developing standard COGS based on expected cost developments.

  • Build a thorough understanding of the warehouse and distribution budget, operational performance and key savings initiatives. 

  • Track whether the expected savings from the recently implemented warehouse and transport provider change are being realized in the P&L. 

  • Further developing cost allocation models for individual markets, using meaningful drivers, and working towards more complete and reliable management reporting.

  • Ensuring the Operations P&L, budget and actual costs are consistently captured and reported in the same structure.

  • Translating inventory developments into financial impact and creating a clear link between stock levels, budget assumptions and cost allocation.

  • Supporting and improving an efficient month-end closing process, ensuring Operations costs are accurately and consistently booked, allocated and reconciled.

  • Establish or improve proper accounting entries together with Finance Administration and relevant operational partners.

  • Co-lead the annual budget cycle and budget presentations to the Board.

  • Using and improving Power BI, ERP data and financial processes to reduce manual work and increase transparency.

You will report directly to the Chief Financial Officer and work closely with colleagues in Finance, Procurement and Operations. You will also have regular contact with the Germany and UK country managers.

This position requires more than strong analytical skills. You will need to explain your insights clearly, engage stakeholders and constructively challenge where necessary. You will be a knowledgeable sparring partner who asks questions, brings structure and takes responsibility from analysis through to implementation. You proactively identify opportunities to improve financial processes, controls, reporting and transparency across Operations.

HG is a compact, fast-growing and international organization where you can directly see the impact of your work. This requires ownership, initiative and a pragmatic, results-oriented mindset. The team culture is open, pragmatic and focused on results, encouraging you to bring ideas forward, challenge constructively and take responsibility. Everything we do is guided by our three core values: Aim High, Be Brave, Be Connected.


What you bring

We are looking for a financially strong, hands-on and improvement-oriented controller who combines analytical capability with a practical understanding of Operations. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across Finance, Procurement and Operations and is able to turn complex cost drivers into clear insights and concrete actions. 

You bring a proactive mindset, strong stakeholder-management skills and a natural drive to simplify and improve processes. You are comfortable challenging existing ways of working, creating structure in a changing environment and taking ownership from analysis through implementation. 

You will also have:

  • A completed university master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or a related field. A Registered Controller (RC) qualification is a strong advantage.

  • Around 10 years of relevant experience in business control, operations control or a comparable financial role.

  • Experience in a manufacturing environment is important, including knowledge of production processes, procurement and cost calculations.

  • A sound understanding of business control, financial controls and treasury.

  • Experience with ERP systems and an understanding of how financial data and accounting flows are structured.

  • Good knowledge of Power BI. You do not need to build everything from scratch, but you can independently investigate, improve and develop analyses.

  • Experience working with consolidation tools.

  • Strong analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills.

  • A proactive, hands-on and improvement-oriented mindset, with the ability to create structure in a changing environment.

  • Fluency in English. Knowledge of Dutch is desirable, and German is an advantage.

  • Experience with AI tools, such as Copilot.

  • Willingness to travel to the United Kingdom and Germany several times a year.

Please note that we do not offer visa or work permit sponsorship for this position. You must therefore hold a valid EU work permit

What do we offer

At HG, you will not be stepping into a role where everything is already set in stone. Changes in our logistics operations, systems and reporting create opportunities to further professionalize financial control and implement improvements yourself.

You can expect:

  • a senior role with broad responsibility and direct influence on financial and operational decision-making;

  • a salary appropriate to the seniority of the role, with an indicative range of €85,000 to €100,000 gross per year;

  • an annual on-target bonus of 25% of your gross annual salary; 

  • full-time employment with 30 days of annual leave; 

  • a pension scheme; 

  • a commuting allowance; 

  • a full-time role based at our head office in Almere. Hybrid working is possible on a limited basis, with office attendance being an important part of the role;

  • a dynamic and ambitious working environment where initiative and ownership are valued;

  • a friendly, welcoming team, with a free shared lunch every Monday and monthly social drinks.
